title: Forensics Logs: Pipeline Failures, Backfill & Retention Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This playbook captures operational guidance for storing, indexing, and restoring security-forensic logs (audit, auth, access events) used for compliance, incident response, and SIEM exports. It focuses on the storage/retention lifecycle, practical backfill approaches, and common pipeline failure modes with runbook steps to remediate.

Context and scope:
- Applies to all system-generated security events ingested by the primary audit pipeline (API gateway, auth service, console, private-deploy agent).
- Not a replacement for policy documents — this is a working operational runbook for SREs and security engineers.
- Retention tiers in scope: hot (0–90d), warm (91–365d), cold (366d–1825d / 5y), and legal-hold/long-term evidence stores (>5y).

Goals / Requirements:
1) Queryability: Recent events (<90d) must support sub-second SIEM queries and replay to detection jobs.
2) Durability: No single-cloud-zone durability loss for any retention tier.
3) Cost-awareness: Backfill and indexing decisions should balance cost and forensic usefulness.
4) Auditability: Every retention and deletion event must be auditable and KMS-wrapped where required.
5) Failure transparency: Pipeline failures must surface actionable alerts with bounded blast radius.

Architecture summary (high-level):
- Ingest: Kafka topic "audit-events" (partitioned by tenant-region). Producers: services emit JSON events with standard schema (see SEC log schema doc).
- Stream processing: Flink job enriches, normalizes (schema vN), and writes to two sinks: 1) hot elasticsearch/Opensearch cluster for <90d fast queries; 2) cloud object store (S3/GS) as compressed daily partitions for archival.
- Index lifecycle manager: ILM policies automatically roll indices to warm and close indices at 90d, snapshot to object store at 180d.
- Cold tier: Data beyond snapshot retention moved to long-term bucket with legal metadata for evidence retention.
- Metadata catalog: BigQuery dataset contains pointers to object-store manifests for quick search of cold partitions (metadata only, not PII).

Retention policies (operational):
- Hot (0–90 days): Fully indexed, searchable, replication factor 2. Retention window enforced by ILM.
- Warm (91–365 days): Read-only indices, reduced replicas, node tiering to warm nodes.
- Cold (366–1825 days): Snapshots in object-store. Metadata in BigQuery. Restore-on-demand via snapshot-restore playbook.
- Legal hold (>5 years or eDiscovery): Copy to isolated evidence-bucket with stricter KMS cmk, immutable object lock where supported. Deletions prohibited unless legal hold removed.
- Deletion: Deletion requests must go via SEC-DELETE workflow and require at least two approvers. Every deletion emits an audit event and retention log.

Indexing and backfill strategies:
- Normal operation: Every incoming event is enriched and indexed in near-real time. The Flink job includes an exactly-once sink semantics to ES.
- Small backfills (last 7 days): Use reingest path: re-produce events to Kafka with replay flag, Flink treats as idempotent (idempotency key = event_id + schema_version).
- Bulk historical backfill (>7 days): Batch transform stored raw events in object-store using Dataflow/EMR job that outputs dated bulk ES bulk-index payloads. Backfill runs against a read-only temporary index alias to avoid disruption.
- Snapshot restore backfill (cold -> hot): Restore snapshots to a temporary cluster and run reindex-from-remote into production indices, throttled by indexers-per-second.
- Backfill validation: After backfill, run a deterministic sampling check: sample N event_ids and verify presence, schema_version, and hash-match between source and index. Store validation report in evidence-buckets.

Common failure modes and remediation steps:
1) Flink task crashes / offset lag grows
   - Symptoms: Monitoring shows high consumer lag on "audit-events", error logs with "OutOfMemory" or checkpoint failures.
   - Immediate action: Restart Flink task via infra-restarts playbook, increase parallelism if CPU saturation, check checkpoint storage latency.
   - Mitigation: If lag > 2h, enable temporary backpressure bypass: stream a sampling of events to an emergency hot-writer that only indexes high-priority audit types (auth, admin_changes).

2) ES cluster write rejections / yellow cluster health
   - Symptoms: Bulk-index errors, increased write latency, cluster status yellow/red.
   - Immediate action: Reduce indexing rate via rate-limiter, trigger index rollover to new index, add warm node capacity OR promote snapshots to restore.
   - If indices corrupted: Stop writes to affected index, take snapshot, create temporary index, reindex from snapshot.

3) Snapshot failures to object-store
   - Symptoms: Snapshot job fails with 403/AccessDenied or partial snapshots.
   - Immediate action: Verify service-account permissions, S3 bucket lifecycle rules, and kms encryption policy. Manually retry snapshot with smaller shard batch.
   - Preventive: Daily snapshot verification job that verifies checksums and manifest completeness. Alert on manifest mismatch.

4) Backfill job timeouts / slowdowns
   - Symptoms: Bulk index tasks time out, CPU on bulk indexers saturated.
   - Immediate action: Reduce bulk size, increase concurrency modestly, or run reindex during off-peak windows.
   - Validation: Always run post-backfill validator; if validation fails, rollback by deleting temp alias and re-run with tighter throttling.

5) SIEM export stalls or duplicates
   - Symptoms: SIEM connector reports duplicate IDs or missed sequences.
   - Immediate action: Check last_sent_cursor in metadata table; reconcile by replaying events from a safe checkpoint.
   - Note: Use idempotent SIEM writes (siem_event_id = event_id) so duplicates are ignored on SIEM side where supported.

Alerting and SLAs:
- Alerts: consumer-lag>30m, es_write_error_rate>1%, snapshot_manifest_mismatch, backfill_validation_fail, siem-export-error. Alerts route to sec-oncall and infra-oncall.
- SLOs: Hot-query availability 99.9% monthly; backfill completion SLA for 30 days of history when requested within 48 hours must be 95% success; evidence-restore SLA for legal-hold requests: 72 hours.

Operational runbook snippets (commands & quick checks):
- Check Kafka lag:
  kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka:9092 --describe --group audit-ingest-consumer
- Restart Flink job (k8s):
  kubectl -n infra rollout restart deployment/flink-audit-processor
- Verify ES cluster health:
  curl -s -u: -XGET "https://es-host/_cluster/health?pretty"
- Trigger manual snapshot:
  curl -XPUT "https://es-host/_snapshot/audit_snap/repo-20250214?wait_for_completion=true" -d '{\"indices\":\"audit-*\"}'
- Validate a backfill sample: run validator job: gsutil cp gs://evidence-bucket/backfills/last-run/report.json ./ && jq .summary report.json

Security & compliance controls:
- All long-term evidence buckets must have object-lock enabled and use a designated legal CMK. Access gated by IAM roles with time-bound session policies.
- Audit of deletions: every retention/expiry event creates a signed manifest and retention event captured in "retention-audits" topic.
- PII handling: cold metadata in BigQuery must strip PII fields. Restores that include PII require additional approvals and temporary sealed environments.

Cost considerations & heuristics:
- Indexing cost is dominant for hot tier; warm nodes save ~45% compute vs hot.
- Backfill cost should be charged to requesting org/team; include credit estimate in backfill request form (see linked Jira ticket).
- Prefer bulk-compressed cold storage for low-access tenants; for high-audit-rate tenants consider extended warm retention.

Playbook for legal/eDiscovery restore:
1) Verify request has legal approval and scope.
2) Create ticket SEC-RESTORE-<id>, attach retention manifest.
3) Create temporary cluster in dedicated VPC with restricted access.
4) Restore snapshots to temp cluster, run validation, export artifacts to sealed evidence-bucket.
5) Log all access and steps to retention-audits topic.

Open questions / pending decisions:
- Exact backup cadence and snapshot frequency for extreme-high-volume tenants (proposal: hourly snapshots for top 3 tenants).
- Automated retention-policy change approvals for customers on Dedicated offering (policy vs manual).
- Concurrency limits for cross-region reindexing during large incident responses.

Appendix: quick links and references
- SEC log schema: https://confluence.redwood/SEC/log-schema-v2
- Evidence retention policy (legal): https://confluence.redwood/Legal/evidence-retention
- Backfill request form: https://forms.redwood/backfill-request

Notes to oncall engineers:
- When in doubt: prioritize integrity of evidence over speed. Make snapshots and preserve manifests before destructive operations.
- Document every manual step in the ticket; these are likely needed for audits.
